question: Which type of mirrors are commonly used in torches, searchlights and vehicle headlights to get powerful parallel beams of light?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Concave mirrors are used to focus light, which helps in producing powerful parallel beams of light.
 
• They have a reflective surface that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• When the light rays parallel to the principal axis fall on a concave mirror, they converge at a single point called the focal point.
 
• This property of concave mirrors makes them ideal for use in devices like torches, searchlights, and vehicle headlights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror:**

 
 
• Convex mirrors have an outward-curved reflective surface.
 
• They diverge light rays, spreading them outwards.
 
• They are used in situations where a wider field of view is needed, such as in rear-view mirrors of vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical Mirror:**
 
 
• Cylindrical mirrors have a reflective surface that curves in only one direction.
 
• They are used in applications requiring the focusing of light along a line, such as in some optical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Bifocal Mirror:**
 
 
• Bifocal mirrors have two distinct optical powers.
 
• They are typically used in eyeglasses to provide both near and distant vision correction.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors have an inward-curved reflective surface.
 
• They converge light rays to a focal point, which helps in creating powerful and focused beams of light.
 
• They are commonly used in applications such as telescopes, shaving mirrors, and flashlights.
